content.content:
Drift is a difference between two owners. jj owns whether a draft's workspace exists: jj is the backend that holds the tree, and a workspace is jj's object. The registry owns what the draft means: the record is the registry's, with its state and the workspace reference it carries. A record names a workspace by name and path, and naming is a reference, not custody — the registry does not create a workspace for a record to name, and does not remove one. Because existence and meaning sit with different owners, the two can disagree, and the disagreement is not a fault in either: nothing in the registry can make jj keep a workspace, and nothing jj holds can tell the registry what the draft meant. That possible disagreement is drift.

An open record whose workspace is gone is drift. Open is the record of a draft that has not landed, and a draft is written in its own workspace, so an open record asserts a draft held in a workspace that jj no longer has. The record still says what it said; the workspace that made it true is absent. That gap between the meaning the registry keeps and the existence jj owns is the difference drift names.

A landed record whose workspace is gone is not drift. Landed is the record of a draft that has landed, and a workspace is where a draft is written; once the draft has landed there is no draft there to write, so the workspace has served its purpose and its absence takes nothing from the record. The landed record is retained past that point, so it outlives the workspace by design: a landed record with no workspace is the normal end of a draft, not a disagreement between the owners.

Reconcile reads the registry against jj's workspaces and reports the drift it finds. It only reads: it changes nothing — no node, no change, no marker — and it does not repair, rewrite, drop, or forget the record. A drifted open record stays exactly as it stands, still open and still naming the workspace it names; the report is the whole of reconcile's effect. What an operator does with the report is not settled here.

Reconcile is therefore not an operation. It is not a creation, a recording, or a removal; it changes no node, no change, and no marker, and it is never bracketed or undone. This is not a separate rule about operations: it is the read-only commitment above, read against the operation boundary recorded elsewhere — an invocation that mutates nothing is not one of the operations that bracket, so there is no marker for it and nothing to undo. This commitment settles no operation unit, no bracketing rule, and no undo rule of its own, and it fixes no verb name and no command surface; the verb and the `drafts` surface that will carry the report are separate commitments decided elsewhere.

These clauses are one commitment. The ownership split is why a difference is possible; the open/landed boundary is where an absence counts as drift; the report is what is done with it; and the refusal to repair is why the report can be the whole of it. Change the first and drift loses its subject, change the second and reconcile reports the wrong records, change the third and nothing is reported, change the fourth and reconcile becomes a repair. They answer one question — what do we do when jj and the registry disagree? — with one answer: report the difference, leave both sides as they stand.
content.rationale:
Drift exists only because two owners hold different halves of a draft. The record is registry-local and names the workspace that holds the draft as a reference, one of the parts it points at rather than something it holds (owyntkvw); jj is the backend that versions the tree and holds the workspaces (xkolyytz); and each draft is written in its own workspace (znskspqs). The registry can therefore say a draft is held somewhere while jj, which alone decides whether a workspace exists, has no such workspace. Nothing in the registry can make jj keep a workspace and nothing in jj can give the record its meaning, so the disagreement is a real state rather than a corruption, and it is exactly the difference that can be reported. That is why the ownership clause cannot be split off: it is what gives a difference two sides to compare.

The record's states decide which absences are drift. Open is the record of a draft that has not landed and landed the record of one that has, and the landed end is retained (vkkwusty). A draft is written in its own workspace (znskspqs), so an open record whose workspace jj no longer has asserts a draft held in a place that does not exist — the difference drift names. A landed draft is not being written anywhere any more, and the retained record outlives the workspace its draft used, so the same absence there is the normal end state, not a disagreement. The open/landed boundary is thus not a second policy: it is the lifecycle read against the same ownership split, and moving it moves the set reconcile reports.

The report is the answer to the only question left: what to do when the two disagree. Reconcile reads the registry against jj's workspaces and states the difference; it changes nothing — no node, no change, no marker — and it does not repair, rewrite, drop or forget the record, so a drifted record stays open and keeps naming the missing workspace. Non-repair is not leniency attached to the report; it is what keeps the report a report. Any repair would have to make one side agree with the other — create a workspace, or rewrite or drop the record — and then there would be no difference left to name; dropping the record is also the one thing the lifecycle's retention says a landed record does not do (vkkwusty). What an operator does with the report is outside this node.

The non-operation statement is the same read-only content read against the operation boundary. An operation is one whole creation, recording or removal (lmwpuqlx); only those bracket, and non-mutating invocations are not operations and never bracket (vwlrqoxk). Reconcile creates, records and removes nothing, so it is not an operation, leaves no marker, and is never bracketed or undone. It is a consequence of the commitment, not a second one: this node settles no operation-unit definition, no bracketing rule and no undo rule, and the verb name and command surface that will carry the report are separate commitments decided elsewhere.
